newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM sees little impact from floods.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM sees little impact from floods.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it expects recent road and railway flooding between its Mount Isa base metals mine and the port of Townsvile, to have only a modest impact on metals production.
"It will have some impact, but it will not be great," MIM spokesman Collin Myers told Reuters.
MIM's deliveries of of copper and zinc concentrate and lead bullion resumed on Monday after being halted late last week when both rail and road links were cut by flood waters following heavy rains.
Transportation from the mine has largely been restored, Myers said.
The rains also occurred during a previously announced partial shutdown of the copper smelter at Mount Isa, which minimised the impact on deliveries, Myers said.
MIM was winding down repair work to a component of smelter, which started on February 20 and was expected to reduce output by about 30 percent for an estimated 25 days.
"The wet occurrred during the repair work, so I guess you could say it was convenient," Myers said.
Myers said the smelter was on track to meet its full year production target of 177,000 tonnes of copper anode.
MIM ships zinc concentrates and lead bullion overseas from Townsville, where it also operates a copper refinery.
